# Input

Figma: [03a. Input](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-896) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-20

A text input field for capturing user-entered data. Built atomically: Label + Field + Helper composed into the Input organism, with the Field molecule wrapping the Value atom plus icon slots. Used everywhere - forms, search, KYC, deal creation.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/input/reference.png`

### Input

The standard bordered single-line text field with label above and helper or error text below. Used across sign-up, KYC questionnaires, beneficiary details and settings.

Level: organism · Contains: Input Label, Input Field, Input Helper Text

Use when:
- Free text such as full name, email, national ID or IBAN in KYC and bank forms
- Any labelled single-line field in a standard bordered form
- Fields that need inline validation messages under the field

Don't use when:
- Phone numbers: use Input Phone
- SAR amounts to invest or withdraw: use Input Amount
- Picking from a closed list: use Select (or Combobox for long lists)
- Multi-line text: use TextArea
- Verification codes: use OTP Input
- Search: use Search Input

Accessibility: Errors go in the helper under the field (linked to it) with a specific message; never mark required in the placeholder.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

### Input Underline

A minimal single-line text field with only a bottom line (and a leading accent on focus) instead of a full border. Used on registration, sign-in and onboarding screens.

Level: organism · Contains: Input Label, Input Underline Field, Input Helper Text

Use when:
- Sign-up and sign-in screens where the form should feel light
- Onboarding steps with one or two fields

Don't use when:
- Standard dense forms such as KYC or bank details: use Input
- Mixing styles in one form: pick Input or Input Underline for the whole form
- Phone number entry: use Input Phone

Accessibility: With no box, the focus accent and red error underline are the only state cues, so always pair error with helper text.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

### Input Label

The text label atom placed above input fields, with an optional red asterisk for required fields.

Level: atom · Part of: Input, Input Underline, Input Phone, Input Amount, Select, Select Underline, Slider Field, Radio Group

Use when:
- Building a custom field layout that needs the standard input label
- Group labels inside Radio Group

Don't use when:
- New form layouts that need a tooltip icon or direction-aware label: use Form Field Label
- A full labelled field: use Input or Form Field instead of assembling atoms

Accessibility: Use Required=true for the visual asterisk and also mark the field required in code.

### Input Helper Text

The small text atom under a field for a hint or a validation error message.

Level: atom · Part of: Input, Input Underline, Input Phone, Input Amount, Select, Select Underline, Slider Field, Radio Group

Use when:
- Hints such as «الحد الأدنى للاستثمار 1,000 ر.س» under a field
- Field-level validation errors: Tone=error

Don't use when:
- Success or info messages with icons: use Form Field Helper
- Form-level or system errors: use Alert or Banner
- Brief confirmations after an action: use Toast

Accessibility: Associate the helper with its field so the error is read when the field gets focus.

### Input Value

The text atom inside a field that shows either the muted placeholder or the typed value.

Level: atom · Part of: Input Field, Input Underline Field

Use when:

Don't use when:

### Input Field

The bare bordered input box (value plus optional leading or trailing icon) without label or helper. It is the default slot inside Form Field and the control for inline edit cells.

Level: molecule · Contains: Input Value · Part of: Input, Form Field

Use when:
- The input slot of Form Field
- Inline edit cells or table filters where the column header acts as the label
- Fields with a leading icon (lock, mail) or trailing action (clear, eye toggle): Icon=leading or trailing

Don't use when:
- A normal labelled form field: use Input or Form Field
- Search boxes: use Search Input
- Minimal underline style: use Input Underline Field

Accessibility: Without its own label it must get an accessible name from the surrounding label or column header.

### Input Phone

A labelled phone number field with a country code prefix (default +966) and the number area. Used for sign-up, KYC, account recovery and beneficiary contacts.

Level: organism · Contains: Input Label, Input Phone Value, Input Helper Text

Use when:
- Sign-up and login by mobile number, for example label «رقم الجوال»
- Recovery contact and KYC contact details

Don't use when:
- Verifying the SMS code sent to that number: use OTP Input
- Other free text: use Input

Accessibility: Use a numeric phone keyboard and keep digits Western (0-9) and left-to-right inside the RTL field.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Input is the foundational text-entry component. Built atomically: three atoms (Label, Helper Text, Value), one molecule (Field), and one organism (Input) that composes them. This separation lets developers reuse the parts independently - Field on its own for compact inline editing, Input for full form layouts with labels.

On Safqah, Input shows up in every form: account creation, deal investment amount, beneficiary details, KYC, transaction notes. Choose Input (organism) for forms with labels. Use Field (molecule) only when you have a custom label treatment (e.g. floating, prefix, inline question).

### At a glance

| Default · waiting | Focused · accepting input | Error · validation failed |
| --- | --- | --- |

### Atomic architecture

Unlike Button or SocialButton, Input is built as a layered system. This makes the parts reusable, the docs scannable, and updates cascade properly: change the Label atom, and every Field/Input that uses it updates automatically.

Atoms - 14 variants across 3 components

The smallest reusable parts. Each handles one piece of typography with bound semantic tokens. Composed into molecules but also usable standalone for custom inline editing patterns.

Input Label · 6 variants

Input Value · 6 variants

Input Helper Text · 2 variants

Molecule - Input Field · 90 variants

Wraps the Value atom in a bordered, padded container with optional leading/trailing icon slots. Handles all visual states (default, active, focus, error, disabled) via bound bg/border/text tokens. Use directly when you need an input control without a label (e.g. inline edit cell, table filter).

Organisms - Input, Input Underline, Input Phone · 90 variants total

Three sibling organisms compose the atoms + molecules in different visual styles. Input (bordered) for standard forms, Input Underline (minimal) for OTP/registration, Input Phone (country code + phone) for phone number entry. Pick the one that matches your use case.

### Anatomy

A complete Input has up to 3 visible parts stacked vertically. The Field can additionally host leading and trailing icons.

| Label (top) Describes what to enter. Required fields show a red asterisk. Uses Input Label atom. Toggle via Show Label boolean prop. | Field (middle) The bordered, padded container holding the value/placeholder. Optional leading or trailing icon slot. State-driven border color via bound border/* tokens. | Value (inside Field) Either placeholder text (gray) or typed value (dark). Uses Input Value atom. Override Value Text prop per instance. | Helper / Error (bottom) Optional supporting text below the field. Neutral tone for hints, error tone for validation messages. Auto-shows on error state. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Sizes

Three sizes match Button conventions for visual consistency in forms. Size carries through Label, Field, Value, and Helper atoms together.

lg

Field 48h · padding 16 · font 16 · icon 20

Primary forms: account creation, deal investment amount, KYC. Most visible - pairs with lg Button. Default for new mobile forms where vertical space allows.

md

Field 40h · padding 12 · font 14 · icon 20

Standard density: settings forms, profile edit, secondary deal info. Pairs with md Button. The most common choice for dense desktop forms.

sm

Field 32h · padding 8 · font 14 · icon 16

Inline edits, table filters, compact dialogs. Pairs with sm Button. Fails WCAG 2.5.5 touch target - only use where tap region is extended.

### States

Five states cover the input lifecycle. Each uses distinct border/text colors to communicate the interaction state without ambiguity.

default

bg/surface · border/default · text/muted

Resting state. White container with subtle gray border. Placeholder text visible.

active

bg/surface · border/strong · text/default

User has typed a value. Stronger border + dark value text. Communicates "this field has content".

focus

bg/surface · border/focus 2dp · text/default

Keyboard focus or tapped. 2dp outset focus ring using border/focus token. Visible against any background.

error

bg/surface · border/error · text/default + error helper

Validation failed. Red border + automatic red error helper below. Use the Helper text prop to set the specific error message.

disabled

bg/disabled · border/default · text/muted

Inert. Gray fill, muted text, no interaction. Use for fields the user cannot edit (system-set, locked, server-managed).

### Icons (Field-level)

The Field molecule supports an optional leading or trailing icon. Icon slot uses INSTANCE_SWAP - drop in any Syntropy icon at instance time. The Input organism inherits the icon settings via the Field instance swap.

none

Default. Just the value/placeholder text. Use for simple text fields where context is clear from the label alone.

leading

Icon on the leading edge (left in LTR, right in RTL). Use for search (magnifier), currency input (currency symbol), or content type cues (mail, lock).

trailing

Icon on the trailing edge. Use for actions (clear X, dropdown chevron, copy), validation indicators (check mark on success), or visibility toggle (eye for passwords).

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Both Input (organism) and Field (molecule) carry a Direction axis. In LTR (English), text aligns left and leading icon sits left. In RTL (Arabic), text aligns right and leading icon sits right - child order is reversed inside the Field so the visual flip is real, not just text-direction.

LTR

Default. Label left-aligned, placeholder/value left-aligned, leading icon on left. Use in English-language contexts.

RTL

Arabic context. Label right-aligned (auto via text direction), placeholder/value right-aligned, leading icon on right. Required for Saudi-facing forms.

### Variant styles - Bordered vs Underline

Input ships in two visual styles for different contexts. Both share the same atomic architecture (Label, Helper, Value atoms) - only the Field treatment differs. Pick the right one based on the surrounding UI density and the input's prominence.

Input · bordered

30 variants · standard form input

Input Underline · minimal

30 variants · OTP, registration, onboarding

### When to use each

Both styles support the same 3 sizes (lg/md/sm), same 5 states (default/active/focus/error/disabled), same RTL/LTR direction axis. The choice is purely visual and contextual.

- Use bordered Input for standard forms: account settings, deal creation, KYC questionnaires, beneficiary forms. The visible border establishes form structure and groups related inputs.
- Use Input Underline for: registration flows, OTP verification screens, sign-in screens, login resend timers, marketing forms. The minimal style focuses attention on the action without competing chrome.
- Don't mix the two styles in the same form. Pick one based on the dominant pattern in the surrounding UI and stick with it for consistency.
- In Arabic/RTL contexts, both styles flip correctly. The Input Underline's leading-edge accent moves to the right side (leading in RTL).

### Phone variant - Country code + phone number

Input Phone is a specialized organism for capturing international phone numbers. It composes the standard bordered Field with a custom Input Phone Value atom that combines a country code prefix (e.g. +966) with a visual separator and the phone number area. Use it anywhere you ask for a phone number - sign-up, KYC, beneficiary entry, recovery contact.

Default country code is +966 (Saudi Arabia) since most Safqah users are Saudi-based. Override the Country code prop per instance for other markets. The country code stays bold and dark across all states because it's a stable identifier - even when the field is disabled or in error, the country context never wavers.

### Anatomy

| Label Standard Input Label atom. "Phone number" or Arabic equivalent "رقم الجوال" depending on locale. | Country code Bold text identifier (e.g. +966, +971, +20). Always uses text/default color regardless of state - it's a stable identifier, not a value to validate. | Separator Thin 1dp vertical line between country code and phone area (border/default). Provides visual grouping without heavy chrome. | Phone number area Placeholder format (5X XXX XXXX) or typed value. Standard Value atom behavior - placeholder muted, typed value dark. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### States

default

active

focus

error

disabled

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Input Phone flips correctly for Arabic contexts. In LTR, the country code sits on the leading edge (left) with the separator to its right. In RTL, the country code moves to the trailing edge (right) with the separator on its left - natural reading order for Arabic users entering their Saudi mobile.

LTR

Default. Country code on left, separator, phone area on right. Country code reads as "+966" naturally before the digits.

RTL

Arabic context. Phone area on left, separator, country code on right. Matches Arabic reading flow - digits in their natural Arabic order, country code as the closing context.

### Show Country boolean

> **Info:** Input Phone exposes a Show Country boolean prop. Default is true - the country code is always visible. Set to false when the country is implied by the surrounding context (e.g. a Saudi-only registration flow where +966 is assumed and the country picker UI is handled separately). When Show Country is false, the field becomes a plain phone number input without the prefix chunk.

### Code examples

```dart
// Saudi mobile number (default)
SafqahInputPhone(
  label: 'Phone number',
  countryCode: '+966',
  placeholder: '5X XXX XXXX',
  size: SafqahInputSize.md,
  onChanged: _onPhoneChange,
)

// UAE mobile (override country)
SafqahInputPhone(
  label: 'Mobile number',
  countryCode: '+971',
  placeholder: '5X XXX XXXX',
  size: SafqahInputSize.md,
  onChanged: _onPhoneChange,
)

// Arabic RTL context
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahInputPhone(
    label: 'رقم الجوال',
    countryCode: '+966',
    placeholder: '5X XXX XXXX',
    size: SafqahInputSize.md,
    onChanged: _onPhoneChange,
  ),
)

// With validation error
SafqahInputPhone(
  label: 'Phone number',
  countryCode: '+966',
  placeholder: '5X XXX XXXX',
  state: SafqahInputState.error,
  helperText: 'Enter a valid Saudi mobile number',
  size: SafqahInputSize.lg,
  onChanged: _onPhoneChange,
)

// Country implied - hide the prefix
SafqahInputPhone(
  label: 'Phone',
  showCountry: false,
  placeholder: '5X XXX XXXX',
  size: SafqahInputSize.md,
  onChanged: _onPhoneChange,
)
```

### Code examples

How to consume Input in production code. The Flutter widget should mirror the atomic architecture: SafqahInputLabel, SafqahInputField, SafqahInput.

### Flutter - basic form input

```dart
// Required field with label, default size
SafqahInput(
  label: 'Email address',
  placeholder: 'name@example.com',
  required: true,
  size: SafqahInputSize.md,
  onChanged: (value) => _email = value,
)

// Field with leading icon (search)
SafqahInput(
  label: 'Search deals',
  placeholder: 'Deal name, sector...',
  leadingIcon: SafqahIcons.search,
  size: SafqahInputSize.md,
  onChanged: _onSearch,
)

// Error state with helper text (validation message)
SafqahInput(
  label: 'Phone number',
  placeholder: '+966 5XX XXX XXXX',
  required: true,
  state: SafqahInputState.error,
  helperText: 'Enter a valid Saudi mobile number',
  size: SafqahInputSize.lg,
  onChanged: _onPhoneChange,
)

// RTL Arabic context
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahInput(
    label: 'البريد الإلكتروني',
    placeholder: 'name@example.com',
    required: true,
    size: SafqahInputSize.md,
    onChanged: (value) => _email = value,
  ),
)
```

### Flutter - Field alone (no label)

```dart
// Inline search bar in a table header
SafqahInputField(
  placeholder: 'Filter by name...',
  leadingIcon: SafqahIcons.search,
  size: SafqahInputFieldSize.sm,
  onChanged: _onFilterChange,
)
```

### React (token-driven)

```dart
<SafqahInput
  label="Email address"
  placeholder="name@example.com"
  required
  size="md"
  onChange={handleEmail}
/>

<SafqahInput
  label="Phone number"
  placeholder="+966 5XX XXX XXXX"
  required
  state="error"
  helperText="Enter a valid Saudi mobile number"
  size="lg"
  onChange={handlePhone}
/>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Form field with validation error: Error state with red border and helper text showing the specific message. User can immediately see what is wrong and how to fix it. Pairs with aria-describedby in code.
- **Don't** · Form field with validation error: Don't leave a failed field in default state. The user submits, gets a generic toast, and has no way to know which field broke validation. Forces guess-and-check.
- **Do** · Required field marking: Required=true shows the red asterisk after the label. Clear visual signal before the user even touches the field. Saves a round-trip with the validator.
- **Don't** · Required field marking: Don't use "(required)" or "(optional)" parens in the placeholder. Placeholder disappears on input; the marking has to be on the label itself.
- **Do** · Disabled vs read-only: Disabled state for fields the user cannot edit at all (system-set values, locked deal info, server-managed fields). Gray bg + muted text communicates inert.
- **Don't** · Disabled vs read-only: Don't use default state for read-only data that looks editable. Users will tap, try to type, and feel the form is broken when nothing happens.
- **Do** · Arabic form - RTL: Direction=rtl flips label alignment, value alignment, and icon position. Required for any Arabic-language Safqah surface (most user-facing forms).
- **Don't** · Arabic form - RTL: Don't use LTR variant in Arabic context. Label aligns left, value aligns left, looks broken in an Arabic-first interface and breaks the reading flow.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for. Input is the most complex component in the Actions+Form families - these notes matter.

> **Warning:** FONT WARNING - Label, Value, and Helper Text atoms use IBM Plex Sans Medium/Regular. The Font/Family/Base variable is broken (resolves to IBM Plex Sans Arabic which is not installed). Same workaround as Button family: I set fontName explicitly. When you reinstall Arabic font + fix the variable, all Input text nodes will need re-binding.

> **Info:** Atomic architecture rationale - separating into Label/Helper/Value atoms + Field molecule + Input organism lets the parts be reused independently. Field on its own = inline edit cell, table filter. Input organism = full form field. Updates to atom typography cascade through the entire system in one edit.

> **Tip:** Show Helper boolean is DECOUPLED from helper.visible at the variant level. The boolean exists for runtime overrides, but the variant master controls default visibility - error variants show helper by default, others hide. This bypasses Figma's "one shared default per property across all variants" constraint that I keep hitting.

> **Warning:** sm size (32 dp) fails WCAG 2.5.5 touch target. The doc Accessibility section flags it. Only use sm where the tap region is extended by a parent (table row click target, inline edit container with padding), never as a standalone primary form input on mobile.

> **Info:** No stroke-width variable in DS - focus ring is raw `strokeWeight: 2`. Same as Button family. When/if a stroke-width primitive is added, rebind all focus rings.

> **Info:** Field state "active" visually shows "Placeholder" text not "Typed value" in the variant reference. This is the combined-set merged TEXT property default issue - Figma merges Value INSTANCE_SWAP defaults across all 90 variants to the first one's default. Visual states (border color, text color) still correctly differ. Users override the Value prop per instance at consumption time anyway.

> **Info:** Input Underline is a sibling organism, not a variant. It lives as its own COMPONENT_SET with its own 30 variants and its own Field molecule (Input Underline Field, 90 variants of its own). It REUSES the Label, Helper Text, and Value atoms - that's the win of atomic architecture. To swap visual styles, swap the entire instance from one organism to the other.

> **Info:** Underline Field uses per-side stroke weights (strokeBottomWeight, strokeLeftWeight) for the underline + leading accent treatment. Active/focus states get a 2dp leading accent; default/error/disabled have no leading accent. The bottom stroke color changes per state via bound border tokens.

> **Info:** Input Phone is a sibling organism alongside Input and Input Underline. All three share the Label and Helper Text atoms. Input Phone uses its own Input Phone Value atom (country code + separator + phone area) instead of the standard Input Value atom - that's the only architectural difference.

> **Info:** Country code is bolded (font/weight/medium) and always uses text/default color regardless of field state. This is a deliberate decision: country code is a stable identifier the user picked once (or the system pre-filled), not a value to validate. Even when the phone number is in error or disabled, the country context never wavers visually.

> **Info:** The visual separator between country code and phone area is a 1dp right-side stroke on the country code chunk (or left-side stroke in RTL). Uses border/default token. Per-side stroke approach matches how Input Underline Field handles its underline + leading accent - consistent with the system.

> **Tip:** Default country code is +966 (Saudi). For multi-region support, override the Country code TEXT prop per instance. For multi-step country picker UX (where the user taps the country code to open a picker), wrap the Input Phone in your own picker logic - the component itself stays presentational.

> **Info:** The dropdown chevron next to the country code is a small SVG vector (drawn as a downward chevron) bound to icon/default token. It scales with size (16dp for lg, 14dp for md, 12dp for sm). It's a visual affordance - when tapping the country chunk should open a country picker. The picker UI is application-level, not component-level - wrap the Input Phone in your own onTap handler.

> **Info:** When Show Country = false, the entire country chunk (text + chevron + separator) disappears via the bound visible property. The phone area expands to fill the available width via auto-layout. No layout shifts or empty space.
